Zoe (People Ops): Quick question  Carlos filed per-diem for a 4-day trip to Seoul but converted all receipts to USD using a manual Google rate. Finance flagged it. Do we require bank conversion rates or is a consistent public rate acceptable?
Carlos: Sorry I did quick conversions. The card showed KRW charges; I used mid-market rate on the day.
Anika: Policy: prefer the bank/card posted conversion when available, because that9s what actually hit your statement. If not available, use the daily official rate (OANDA/ECB) but please note the source in the expense comment.
Finance Ops: Confirmed. If card statement shows a USD posting use that. If your receipts are cash in local currency and no card txn, use OANDA rate for the date and include a line: "Conversion method: OANDA on 2026-05-10". Attach screenshots showing rate.
Currency Bot: Tip: attach a screenshot of the bank statement showing the posted USD amount or a screenshot of the OANDA rate page with date. Filenames should include date and vendor, e.g., 2026-05-10-seoul-dinner-rate.png.
Carlos: For per-diem we claim a flat local rate each day  do we convert per-diem totals or individual day receipts?
Zoe (People Ops): Convert each day's items using that day's rate. For per-diem line items, indicate day-by-day conversion or attach a simple table in the expense comment.
Anika: Also: if reimbursement differences are > $10 due to conversion method, include manager approval explaining chosen method.
Finance Ops: We'll accept either: (1) bank posted USD amounts, or (2) OANDA/ECB daily rate with screenshot + comment. Do not use proprietary hand-rolled spreadsheets without source.
Carlos: Got it. I1ll re-submit with the card posted amounts where available and OANDA screenshots for cash purchases. Thanks.
Zoe (People Ops): I1ll add a one-liner to the receipts wiki: "For foreign currency claims prefer bank/card posted USD amounts; otherwise use a documented public daily rate (OANDA/ECB) and attach screenshot. Convert per diem/receipts by day; manager note required if conversion choice materially affects reimbursable amount." :memo:
